questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: go through course catalogue, register for courses, see which you get accepted into. if you get placed on waiting list you can show up to first class adn ask professor if there is space. you can also deregister if you regret signing up for a course

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: info online

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: very successful. i signed up for way more than required and planned it well so there was not a lot of overlaps

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: do the above mentioned

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.answer: Both

questions.answer: ba courses were pretty easy, ma courses were harder but still managable

questions.answer: the mediation competition, because it was fun and very practical. it includes traveling, great way to meet austrian students, competitions were very fun and a good way to lean negotiation and mediation. also, introduction to negotiation, very practical and fun

What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: usi has all kinds of sports. esn has all kinds of events, such as wine and hike, day and weekend trips, beer pong tournament, architecture tours, coffee and run, etc.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: all of them to meet different people

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: trips to the mountains, wine and hike, donau, museums, theaters, cinema, bars, cafes

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: doing a class that rwquires woking with austrian students. otherwise, asking them if they wanna grab a beer of a cofeee

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: i found them less direct/honest

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: they are easy going and chill imo

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. this is an opportunity to try doing things differently
2. say yes as much as possible
3. meet as many people as possible in the beginning

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: check out events in vienna, book opera early on

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: meeting so many sweet people and experiencing so much in a short time

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: arriving to a city where you dont know anyone or the city itself. it felt lonely but pushed me to go out and meet new people

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
